Then a person jumped out of the car, and starting cursing me. And later, he called the police saying I drove too fast. I am still mad of this person.

I was deeply offended when someone told me was bashing my candidate for an election for financial officer. I felt that they made assumptions that were not based and were just for mudslinging. It got some other people pretty upset as well.

In one of my classes, this girl was talking about how her roommate is an engineering major and she was complaining about how her roommate had to stay up until 3am the night before doing a problem set. She was ranting about why these engineering majors/techies waste their time staying up and doing problem sets and studying and saying that it was completely useless and irrelevant. I was offended by her statement because I have taken a lot of techie classes and people put a lot of work into it, sometimes liking it a lot. She had a very biased view as a fuzzy.

When members of my sorority felt that I was not a good leader or role model to represent the sorority.  They did not tell me to my face, but rather talked about me behind my back and did not address any issues that were bothering them.

how could they have done that to me? It could have ruined a lot of things for me. They surely are not perfect themselves... Anyways, this was done and now I know humans are not to be trusted. You can only trust the one who created the universe

In high school, I lived in the same dorm as a kid named Jake. At the time, I had a number of good friends who I hung out with very often. For some reason, Jake took it upon himself to talk badly about me to all my friends behind my back, while maintaining a friendly exterior to me - thus fooling me into thinking he couldn't possibly be doing the things he was doing. Eventually, he managed to turn most of my friends against me, which led to a rather miserable high school experience for me

I was offended when another person (a male) called me ugly in middle school. This incident was deeply troublesome because my best friend did not stand up for me at the time. She had a crush on this guy and continued to like him/hang out with him even after he called me names.

My girlfriend, with whom I was in a long term relationship, cheated on me before we broke up. At the time I was extremely forgiven, but since then I have come to resent her at the end, and have cut myself off from her. She betrayed our trust and was not ready for that type of relationship.

I am upset that a friend assumed that I did not care about her and was being malicious when my actions - albeit somewhat thoughtless - were mostly just because I was very busy at the time. I wish she had discussed the issue with me from the beginning rather than letting resentment build up and then taking it out on me in what I saw as an unfair situation.

I was given the wrong impression by a girl who I thought wanted to be my friend, but then she randomly decided to stop talking to me for no reason. I still don't understand why. It really annoyed me and it still does.

One time an individual sent me a very rude email criticizing my choice of speaker for an event I had planned at Stanford campus. The individual did not approve of the individual's political affiliations and criticized me for bringing someone who was against my group's mission, even though my group and everyone who attended the event was pleased with the speaker.

I felt deeply hurt when my best friend had just gotten back from a long trip away and asked me to pick her up from the airport; then as soon as she got in the car, she asked me whether I could take her to the train station so she could go spend the evening with her boyfriend. I normally would have been completely supportive had I been given a heads up, but I had made a lot of plans for us to spend time together and felt hurt just to be asked for a ride, but not wanted to spend time with. In the end, we talked about it because I think she realized, so everything is fine now. It just made me feel very disappointed at the time.

I was riding my bicycle between my dorm and the gym. My headlight was just stolen. The policyman called me up and said I need to be fined because I didn't have a headlight on my bike. I said I feel really bad about getting it stolen as well, and I will buy it immediately. But he said no and he gave me the ticket. In the process, he appeared to be really threatening to me.

My coach did not trust me and accused me of not being fully engaged and devoted to my sport and my team. She and I disagreed a lot and did not get along. She has embarrassed me publicly. She talks behind my back and puts other people against me.

I was deeply offended when my fifth grade teacher scolded me in front of the full class and made me walk out of the class. I still believe I was not treated fairly. As a result, I have some anger towards that person.

I was deeply offended by a stranger in high school who called me "forever nerd" and "silly Asian" because I always had study group after school with some of my best Asian friends. Even though I did work very hard in school, I also spent time having fun outside of time and on weekend. Just because this person didnt know well about my personal life, he assumed that all I did was studying and reading books.

All throughout my childhood, my mother was somewhat critical of me regarding skills, food, capabilities, etc. She would say things like, "I think that's enough..." after 5 spoons of ice cream and then push the bowl away. Or 'You did this wrong!' As a result, I have carried some resentment and shame with me as I've grown up.

My freshman year, I was a part of a student group that was planning a big event.  We had four committee chairs (of which I was one) and one event chair who was supposed to oversee all of our committee activities.  However, as the quarter and event planning progressed, our event chair kept missing meetings, and the four of us committee chairs did most of the planning ourselves, working together.  However, as the event neared, the event chair came to one of our meetings and wanted to assert his authority as the event chair, acting like he knew what was going on and like he still had authority over our dealings.  When our staff advisor spoke to him privately and asked him to step down as event chair since he wasn't meeting his duties, he didn't seem to understand why.  Later, he went on to be involved in student government, and would tout his successes as part of that student group, even though in my mind I did not see him as hard-working or competent.

I got really offended when this friend of friend I barely knew replied to one funny video I posted on his facebook wall (just a cartoon with a guy entering a shop selling shoes that make noise and the shoes he bought would go "ooh baby" whenever he takes a step) with a super angry email, accusing me to accuse him of cheating on his girlfriend. Indeed the night before, when I met him, he was flirting with a girl, but obviously it is none of my business and since I did not know him, nor the girl, nor his girlfriend, I really did not give a damn of whether he cheated or not. In fact, I just posted the video innocently, because we told about that series of videos at that party. So I replied very clearly and angrily that he offended me by thinking I am such a jerk to post gossipy allusion on his publicly accessible fb wall when I barely know him!

I was pretty mad when my friends convinced me to go to a party for the first time on our graduation night, and then pretty much left me there on my own. And then the next morning I found out that someone threw up on my car.

My ex-boyfriend wrote a blog post about me and how it hurt him that I said in a chat the night before something along the lines of: "he's like you, but better" in reference to someone I was checking out. It hurt me deeply because we were on good terms as exes before that moment, and he should have stopped me during the conversation to acknowledge that those were hurtful words (because now that I look back on it, they were).

A friend of mine had soiled my favorite shirt. I accosted him and in return he got angry at me saying I was in the middle as he was trying to do the same thing to a guy behind me. When I asked him to apologize, he didn't and started getting angry at me. I felt he was acting totally like an irrational person and hence I still have some anger towards him.

It was a group brainstorm session. I was talking about some points and then a girl disrupted me and moved on to what she thought was important and brilliant. I was just ignored. I felt upset about her doing so. Because first it's not polite, and second it made me feel powerless and useless in a new environment.

To be honest, I rarely feel deep offense toward another person-- so I truly cannot remember a specific time I felt this way.  I believe that it is one's choice to be offended-- offense can be inflicted by another person, but we choose how we will react.  And I choose to not be offended :)

I have known a friend since middle school. As of late, we have not talked often due to distance and everyone is just busy with their own lives. Our birthdays are three days apart, but I still invited her out for dinner and celebrations. She did not do the same for me. I felt hurt and somewhat betrayed.

To be honest, I've been lucky to have not been offended in some time and that comes down to people here being very respectful and my avoiding potential situations. In high school I would say it happened among and with my friends, but that's part of maturing.

I was deeply hurt when my dad caused a scandal in front of my family when he was drunk. I was also deeply humiliated because he was screaming at my mom, at my brothers, and at me. I had never seen my dad act this way and it was all because he drank too much. The reason why he got so upset was because he wanted us to go home in his car, which had no lights and we were traveling by night. This to me was a dumb reason to get upset over.

Last night, a friend and I got into an argument.  She seemed irritated with me and had absolutely no reason to be.  I let her know that it hurts when she treats me that way and left.  I'm still pissed off  this morning.

an acquaintance said i seem undesirable to the opposite sex, but once he realized what he said, tried to backtrack and take it back. hearing that honesty was painful and i've tried to avoid him since that incident

I was eating lunch with my (mostly male) friends when I was talking about the graduate student I was dating, and how I didn't think I liked him but I was still going on dates because I wasn't sure about what I thought and wanted to give him a chance.  Then they started joking that I was a terrible person for leading him on, and kept saying things like that I was a gold-digger, or ripped out men's hearts for fun.  One acquaintance even went so far as to blame me and women like me on campus for the reason he doesn't have a girlfriend.  I was really hurt by these accusations, but even more so that my friends did not stand up for me.

There was a time when one of my mentors, who I respected, assumed that because I came from a home with a single parent that I must have had a incomplete or deficient childhood. I was frustrated not only because it came from him but also because it made me think that this pity characterized his interaction with his patients. I still get angry whenever I think about it.

I was deeply hurt by a friend who neglected me to hang out with her boyfriend. We had scheduled a dinner and she stood me up to go on a date with her boyfriend who had asked her out after I did. I felt hurt and sad and lonely

When I was younger, my brother and I fought a lot. It was usually the normal type of fighting between kids (bickering, punches) but one day it was different. My brother (my twin, so the same age) was angry that I was a Christian. He called me stupid, and started punching me really hard. I fell, and he kicked me repeatedly, telling me to stop being religious. I stayed quiet until he stopped and left.

When my significant other took his brother to his company holiday party instead of me. What made it worse was how he acted like they had such a great time afterward. I haven't felt bad like that since, but that was pretty bad.
